Licence classes

The four classes that actually trade in San Francisco

California numbers its licence types, and the number decides what you may pour, to whom, and whether you need a kitchen. Four of them change hands here often enough to have a market. Each has its own page below, with its stock priced.

    • Type 47
    • Quota class

    On-Sale General, Eating Place

    A restaurant with a full bar. Beer, wine and distilled spirits poured for drinking on the premises, in a room that serves real meals from a real kitchen. California calls that a bona fide public eating place, and the kitchen is not a formality: lose it and you lose the licence.

    It is the deepest class in San Francisco by a distance, and the one most buyers are actually looking for when they say “a liquor licence”.

    • On our San Francisco book18

    • Range$135,000–$350,000
    Type 47 in San Francisco
    • Type 21

    Off-Sale General

    A liquor store, spirits included. Beer, wine and distilled spirits sold sealed, to be drunk somewhere else. This is the off-sale class that carries spirits, and it is under the county quota exactly as the on-sale general classes are.

    Ten on the book, and the widest price spread of any San Francisco class — location and trading history move an off-sale licence more than they move an on-sale one.

    On-Sale General, Public Premises

    A bar or nightclub, over-21 only. The same drinks as a Type 47 and none of the kitchen obligation — but nobody under 21 may enter and remain, which rules out families, all-ages shows and most daytime food trade.

    Genuinely rare on the open market here: one on our book, and one in the whole San Francisco County catalogue we measured.

The mechanism

Why a San Francisco licence costs what it costs

California does not issue general licences on demand. The number of on-sale general licences — the Type 47 and Type 48 classes — is limited against county population, and so is the number of off-sale general licences, the Type 21 class. San Francisco has been over both ceilings for decades. The Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control does not issue new originals here, so the only way to get one is to buy one from somebody who already holds it.

That is the whole price mechanism, and it explains the two things that surprise buyers most. First, why the price is not a business valuation. You are not buying revenue, a lease, a kitchen, a customer list or a name. You are buying a transferable permission, and everything that makes it earn money you supply yourself. Second, why the spread is so wide: $15,000 to $350,000 on the same 30-licence book. The spread is not quality. It is which side of the quota line the class sits on.

Look at the two ends. The Type 20 at the bottom is off-sale beer and wine, and it is not quota-limited — ABC will issue a new one to a qualified applicant. Nobody pays a fortune for something they can apply for. The Type 47 at the top is quota-limited and there is no queue to join: when San Francisco restaurants want a full bar, the only supply is the licence somebody else is giving up. Same city, same paperwork, a twenty-three-fold difference in price, and the quota explains all of it.

It also explains why San Francisco has a second clock that most states do not. Getting the licence transferred is one process, with ABC. Getting your address approved to use it can be a second one, with San Francisco Planning, if your Neighborhood Commercial District requires a conditional use for the alcohol use you have in mind. The two run at different speeds, and the Planning one is usually slower. Anybody quoting you a San Francisco timetable without asking for your address is quoting you half the job.

Honest gap: the quota is set by ratio in the Business and Professions Code — roughly one on-sale general per 2,000 county residents and one off-sale general per 2,500 — and the operative sections sit in the §23816 to §23817 range. We have given you the mechanism rather than a section number we would want counsel to confirm. Read the code, or ask us and we will get the current citation from ABC counsel rather than guess at it.

The fifth class, and why it has no page here

Type 41 — On-Sale Beer and Wine, Eating Place

A Type 41 lets a bona fide eating place serve beer and wine with meals. No spirits, no cocktail list, and the same real-kitchen obligation a Type 47 carries. For a great many San Francisco restaurants it is the right licence and nobody tells them so, because it is the one nobody makes money selling.

The reason is the quota. A Type 41 is not quota-limited. If you qualify and your premises is approved, ABC will issue you a new one — you apply, you pay the fee, you wait out the posting period. There is no scarcity to arbitrage, so there is almost no resale market, and there is no San Francisco Type 41 stock on our book to price. Buying one second-hand would mean paying a premium for something the state will sell you directly.

So the honest advice is the advice that loses us the sale. If your concept works on beer and wine, apply for a Type 41 and keep the six figures. Come back to a Type 47 when a cocktail programme is genuinely load-bearing for the room — and be aware that upgrading later means buying a Type 47 on the open market at whatever it costs then, not converting the licence you hold.

Why this is a section and not a page. We hold no San Francisco Type 41 stock and there is nothing to price, so a Type 41 page would be a page about a thing we cannot sell you. It lives here instead, next to the classes that do trade, where somebody choosing between them will actually read it.

OursThe recommendation above is our commercial judgement, not a regulatory statement. MeasuredThere is no San Francisco Type 41 stock in the open market catalogue we read on 13 September 2026.

How a transfer works

From accepted offer to trading, in 78 days

That is the median across our 64 closed California files. The stages below are the medians for each step and they add to the same 78 days. Nothing here is quick, and thirty of those days are a statutory posting period that nobody can shorten — anyone promising you a four-week San Francisco transfer is describing paperwork, not the calendar.

  1. Offer accepted, escrow opened7 days

    A purchase agreement, then escrow with a licensed escrow holder. California requires the full consideration to sit in escrow before the Department will approve the transfer, so this is the point your money moves, not completion day.

  2. Buyer qualification and application10 days

    The person-to-person transfer application, Live Scan fingerprinting for every principal, and proof of funds. This is also when the mutual NDA is signed and the confidential file — licence number, licensee of record, premises address, term, encumbrances, tax position — is released to you.

  3. Public notice posted at the premises30 days

    ABC posts the application at the premises for 30 days, and the notice of intended transfer is published in a newspaper of general circulation. The 30 days are statutory and cannot be shortened, whatever anyone promises you.

  4. Protest period and local agency review14 days

    Any protest filed during the posting is worked through here, and this is where San Francisco can add time: the Police Department’s alcohol liaison reviews on-sale applications, and a Planning conditional use, if your district needs one, runs on its own much longer calendar.

  5. ABC investigation and approval10 days

    The investigator confirms the premises, the qualification of the buyer and the tax position of the seller. Clean files clear here without anyone hearing from anyone.

  6. Escrow closes, licence issued in your name7 days

    Approval issued, escrow released to the seller, licence recorded against you. You can trade.

SampleStage day counts are invented for this mockup but internally consistent: 7 + 10 + 30 + 14 + 10 + 7 = 78, matching the stated median. OursThe 30-day posting is a statutory period; the rest is our reading of how San Francisco files actually run.

Costs

What a transfer costs on top of the price

Most liquor licence marketplaces publish a price and stop there. Here is the rest of the bill, worked on the median San Francisco licence, so you can budget before you enquire rather than after.

Estimated buyer-side costs to complete a San Francisco transfer, excluding the price of the licence itself. Untick anything you will handle yourself and the total re-adds. Scroll sideways on a narrow screen.
Include Cost Paid to Amount
Escrow fee Licensed escrow holder, as Bus. & Prof. Code §24074 requires $1,450
ABC person-to-person transfer fee California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control $1,250
Notice of intended transfer, published Newspaper of general circulation in San Francisco $385
Live Scan and fingerprinting, two principals California Department of Justice, via ABC $160
Buyer’s counsel, ABC transfer work Your attorney $4,800
Total cost to close, excluding the price $8,045
This licence plus costs to close $213,045
  • The whole price goes into escrow, not a deposit. This is the part that surprises buyers coming from other states. California requires the full consideration for a licence transfer to be placed with a licensed escrow holder before the transfer is approved, and it is released to the seller only on issue. There is no 10% and no balance on completion.
  • Conditional use, where San Francisco requires it. A change of licence or a new alcohol use in many of the city’s Neighborhood Commercial Districts needs Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission before ABC will act. Budget $3,000 to $8,000 and three to five months for that track, and treat it as separate from the figures above. It is the single largest source of San Francisco timetable slippage.
  • After you hold it: the ABC annual renewal on a San Francisco on-sale general licence runs about $1,400, and about $700 on an off-sale.
  • Our commission: 4% of the accepted price, paid by the seller at closing. There is no buyer-side fee, no registration fee and no charge for the confidential file once you are qualified.
  • Financing: a licence is not mortgageable the way real property is, and most California lenders will not lend against one alone. We work with two lenders who underwrite licence transfers as part of a wider fit-out facility and will make an introduction.

Released when you qualify

The licence number and the address are not on this page

Not masked, not blurred, not shown in part. They are simply not published, for any licence, anywhere on this site — and neither is any photograph of a licensed premises. A seller is almost always still trading. In a city where a neighbourhood and a licence class narrow a business to a handful of doors, publishing either one tells their staff, their landlord and the operator across the street that they are selling. So the shop window carries everything you need to shortlist, and nothing that identifies the seller.

Sign a mutual non-disclosure agreement and the complete file is released to you within one business day. There is no fee for it. Four further San Francisco licences are held entirely off-market at the seller’s request and are only ever shown this way — they are not among the 30 on the book.

Activity, honestly

Dates, yes. Counters, no.

Every listing above carries the day it came to market and how long it has sat there. That is a fact we can stand behind, and on this book it ranges from 3 days to 102. What you will not find anywhere on this site:

  • ×No view count. A view count is trivially inflated and proves nothing about demand.
  • ×No watcher count and no “3 people are looking at this right now”.
  • ×No bid ticker, no auction clock, no countdown. Offers are reviewed as they arrive.
  • ×No manufactured scarcity. The county quota supplies all the scarcity this market needs.

MeasuredWhy we bother saying so: of the 1,227 listings on the largest rival liquor licence marketplace, not one carries a date of any kind. Their view counters are bounded 0–36 with every integer present and no relationship to listing age; one listing shows more bids than views. Only 28 of the 1,227 have ever taken a bid. The counters are decoration.

Questions

San Francisco liquor licences, answered plainly

How much does a liquor license cost in San Francisco?

Across the 30 San Francisco licences on our book the median ask is $205,000, inside a range of $15,000 to $350,000. The class is what moves it: a Type 47 eating-place licence runs a $232,500 median, a Type 21 off-sale $175,000, and the single Type 20 sits at $15,000 because it is the only class on the page that is not quota-limited. The price is for the licence alone — no premises, no fixtures, no goodwill — and completing costs about $8,045 on top.

Why are San Francisco liquor licenses so expensive?

Because supply is fixed by statute rather than by demand. California limits on-sale general licences (Types 47 and 48) and off-sale general licences (Type 21) against county population, and San Francisco has been over both ceilings for decades. No new originals are issued here, so the only route in is to buy an existing one. Classes that sit outside the quota — Type 41 and Type 20 — are cheap for exactly the same reason, in reverse.

How long does a liquor license transfer take in San Francisco?

A median of 78 days across our 64 closed California files, from accepted offer to a licence issued in your name. Thirty of those days are the statutory posting period at the premises and cannot be compressed by anyone. The figure assumes your address is already cleared for the use — if your Neighborhood Commercial District requires Conditional Use Authorization from San Francisco Planning, add three to five months for that track, running on its own calendar.

Do I pay a deposit, or the whole price?

The whole price. This catches out buyers who have done a transfer in another state. California requires the full consideration for a licence transfer to be placed with a licensed escrow holder before the Department will approve it, and it is released to the seller only when the licence issues. There is no 10% down and no balance on completion — the money sits in escrow for the length of the process.

What is the difference between a Type 47 and a Type 48?

Both permit beer, wine and distilled spirits for consumption on the premises. A Type 47 is tied to a bona fide eating place: a real kitchen serving real meals, and if the food operation stops the licence is at risk. A Type 48 is a public premises licence with no food obligation at all — and the trade-off is that nobody under 21 may enter and remain, which closes off families, all-ages events and most daytime food trade. Pick on the room you intend to run, not on the price.

What is the difference between a Type 21 and a Type 20?

Both are off-sale: sealed, taken away, not drunk on the premises. A Type 21 carries distilled spirits and is quota-limited, which is why ten of them are on this book at a $175,000 median. A Type 20 is beer and wine only and is not quota-limited, which is why the single one here asks $15,000. If your shop does not need spirits, the Type 20 route is an application to ABC rather than a purchase, and we will tell you so.

Is San Francisco a city or a county for licensing?

Both, and that is why this is one page rather than two. San Francisco is a consolidated city and county: the city and the county are the same jurisdiction with the same boundary and the same quota. A “San Francisco city” licence and a “San Francisco County” licence are the same thing. Anyone showing you separate city and county inventory for San Francisco is showing you the same licences twice.

Do I need approval from the City as well as from ABC?

Often, yes, and it is the step that sets the timetable. ABC handles the licence. San Francisco Planning handles whether an alcohol use is permitted at your address, and in many Neighborhood Commercial Districts a new or changed alcohol use needs Conditional Use Authorization from the Planning Commission. Some districts restrict off-sale licences further still. The Police Department’s alcohol liaison also reviews on-sale applications. Tell us the address before you sign a lease, not after.

Why is the license number and premises address not published?

Because the seller is almost always still trading. Publishing the licence number, the licensee of record, the trading name or the address tells their staff, their landlord, their suppliers and the operator across the street that the business is for sale. In a city this size a neighbourhood alone would do it, which is why we do not publish that either — every listing here says San Francisco and stops. The full file is released to a qualified buyer under a mutual NDA, at no charge, within one business day.

Do you charge buyers a fee?

No. Our commission is 4% of the accepted price, paid by the seller at closing. There is no buyer-side commission, no registration fee, no charge for the confidential file and no charge for a lender introduction. You will pay your own counsel, the escrow holder, ABC and the publisher of the notice — about $8,045 in total — and nothing to us.

Design review note — not part of the live page

This one page replaces thirteen

San Francisco is currently answered by thirteen live addresses across two competing path sets — six under /cities/san-francisco/ and seven under /counties/ — describing the same consolidated jurisdiction and competing for the same queries. All thirteen return HTTP 200 with no redirects. Between them they hold 9 ranked keywords and 4.2 modelled monthly visits, best absolute position 10.

  • ×The rival answers the same city with one page: 4 ranked keywords, 22.2 modelled visits, positions 3, 3, 4 and 10. One page beats thirteen by 5.3× — per page, by 69×.
  • ×The client’s city-type pages carry a median 895.5 unique words against 339 on the rival county pages that outrank them. They write 2.6× more and lose. This is not a content quality problem.
  • ×The cannibalisation is visible in the ranking data: the generic query liquor license san francisco is answered at position 13 by the Type 48 bars and nightclubs page, not by any hub. san francisco liquor license → Type 48 at 18. sf liquor license → Type 48 at 21. The narrowest page is fielding the broadest queries.
  • ×Defects carried live: the county hub has no H1 at all and an empty meta description; the county licences page has its H1 text doubled inside one element; and San Francisco County Type 47 is filed under the Los Angeles County folder.

Thirteen addresses become five: this hub and four licence-class pages, each justified by real San Francisco stock — 18, 10, 1 and 1. Type 41 gets no page because there is no San Francisco Type 41 stock and neither existing Type 41 page ranks for anything; it is a section on this page instead.
